steps.title: -er verbs: parler, habiter, s'appeler
steps.body: Most French verbs end in -er. They are regular. Remove -er, then add the endings:

steps.title: The first three persons (we, you-plural and they come in Unit 4)
-er verbs: parler, habiter, s'appeler
steps.body:
• The endings -e, -es, -e are silent: parle, parles and parle all sound the same (pahrl).
• Only the pronoun tells you who is speaking. This is the silent-letter rule from Stage 0.
• s'appeler literally means to call oneself. Je m'appelle Sam = I call myself Sam. The m' is me reduced (élision).
